body:
## Problem

Replay support checks often reduced known Vulkan features, extensions and limits to “not supported,” while failed dependencies obscured why downstream pipelines were never created. One warning per object could flood logs on large captures.

## What changes

Preserves caller-owned support details and source dependency identities through parsing and scheduling. Known compatibility boundaries and originating read, parse, creation and support failures remain distinct from consumers whose dependencies prevented creation.

Replaces targeted per-object support/dependency prose with cause counts and representative examples. Groups identify the unsupported feature, extension, property, capability or constraint; distinct nested constraints such as attachment and subpass flags have distinct names. Examples retain resource hashes and known required/available values, and blocked consumers carry known originating support causes when retained.

Each worker attempt retains at most **32 cause groups**, **two examples per group and eight examples overall**. Its targeted report is bounded to **42 warning lines and 32 KiB**, including an overflow observation count. Reports flush once after producers drain, including ordinary early failure and standalone operation. Quiet workers remain quiet and protocol stdout is preserved.

Adds real-stderr volume, grouping, dependency, concurrency, lifecycle, compatibility and worker tests, documentation and an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Why this matters

Large captures produce useful cause counts and a few examples instead of thousands of repeated support warnings. Users can distinguish blocked consumers from driver compilation failures.

## Why this approach

Existing bool callers and support decisions remain compatible. Fixed storage bounds diagnostic retention and report size; semantic grouping excludes varying object hashes and requested limit values. Structured worker diagnostics remain independent of human log verbosity.

## Verification and limits

Reviewed head: `c57dfc70b6a1f2abdbefb31aa0c90ba4a6ce3c94`.

- Independent unit checker: **282/282 tests in each of four Linux Debug/Release × exceptions OFF/ON configurations**, with CLI/layer/SPIR-V validation enabled and runtime-layer testing disabled.
- Focused ASan+UBSan: **38/38**, with actual instrumentation verified. Eight concurrency cases passed three times each. Four independently compiled controls caught lost support details, lost dependency identity, restored per-object warning spam and collapsed constraint identities; the strict verifier passed.
- Separate final checker: **153/153 decisive tests in both Debug/OFF and Release/ON**, including all eight warning-output cases; two additional compatibility checks passed in each configuration, and eight concurrency cases passed three times each.

[Independent unit evidence](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/harness-artifacts/runs/issue-19/issue19-text-warnings-20261110/reports/text-checker-repair-1.json) and [separate final evidence](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/harness-artifacts/runs/issue-19/issue19-text-warnings-20261110/reports/text-checker-final-3.json) retain exact bindings, commands, outcomes and all 23 case mappings. The detected same-resource constraint grouping collision was repaired and independently rechecked; superseded readiness and evidence-verifier setup failures remain preserved.

Counts are replay observations within one worker attempt, including repeats; they are not globally unique pipeline counts. Excess groups contribute to the overflow observation count without claiming omitted-cause cardinality. Long identifiers explicitly truncate and may coalesce beyond the retained prefix; saturation is marked as a lower bound. Bounded dependency context may leave a support cause unknown.

The cap applies to the replaced support/dependency report. Unrelated parser, validation-policy/blacklist, allocation and driver diagnostics keep their existing behavior and can still be numerous. Hard exits and crashes do not guarantee a completed summary.

Native Windows verification was explicitly waived and remains unverified. CPU fixtures do not establish GPU, Steam, driver-cache or persistence behavior, or a general prebuilt binary ABI guarantee. An earlier head's inherited timeout-status assertion failure and successful retries remain in the [original run evidence](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/harness-artifacts/runs/issue-19/issue19-20261110/reports/checker-unit-3.json); they are not current-head results, and the original native status remains unknown.

## Task references

Closes https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/19

Shared requirements: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8 (remains open).
